title: Single-grid results, connectivity and ParaView Warp
summary: Keep topology and field ordering inside the output backend. The serial ResultWriter stores one grid per time with complete point/cell attributes, rejecting invalid frames before storage; ParaView Warp needs no duplicate-block cleanup.

science.statement: Connectivity encodes the finite-element topology in the target reader's ordering. A field must be transferred through its basis and entity identity, not matched solely by coefficient count.

equations.label: display coordinates
equations.description: Warp adds a scaled nodal displacement to reference coordinates; applying it again to deformed coordinates double-counts motion.

inputs.name: mesh and fields
inputs.description: One nodal scalar/vector primary, compatible continuous auxiliary fields or explicit DG0 cell fields.

outputs.name: visualization artifact
outputs.type: single-grid serial XDMF/HDF5 or collective PVD
outputs.description: One geometry per saved time with attached point/cell fields and a known geometry convention.

assumptions: The serial unified series retains one mesh and primary function space.
Cell array keys are original input cell indices, not external element labels.
conventions: Prefer step.solve_result(output=...) for the ordinary result lifecycle; use io.ResultWriter only for explicit custom export.
Do not hand-write connectivity, guess VTK permutations, or merge coincident crack/interface nodes to repair visualization blocks.
Use the manifest's recommended_visualization_artifact under MPI; low-level DOLFINx XDMF can contain one block per field.
Frame times must be finite and strictly increasing; names, associations and shapes must remain stable.
Duplicate names and nonfinite fields fail before frame storage. A storage failure requires a new artifact.
Reference geometry uses Warp once. Already deformed presentation geometry requires no additional Warp.
Discontinuous cell fields are not automatically smoothed across material interfaces.
applicability: Human- and AI-authored static/transient result export, finite-element visualization and repair of synchronous single-mesh DOLFINx archives.
limitations: Presentation checks do not establish physical accuracy.
Serial ResultWriter write mode is single-grid; legacy append and MPI scientific XDMF retain distinct contracts.
Unsupported topology, cross-mesh transfer and raw integration-point interpretation are not inferred.

usage.minimal_example:
result = step.solve_result(output='fields.xdmf')
# For custom serial exports:
with io.ResultWriter('custom.xdmf', domain, (u, stress_cell)) as writer:
    writer.write(physical_time)

validation_rules: Read exported Hex/Tet fields through independent VTK readers and compare warped coordinates.
Compare equal-size fields with different nodal variants against physical coordinates after interpolation.
Reject invalid frames without leaving partially written groups; reject reuse after storage failure.
Verify unchanged reference geometry shares HDF5 storage across frames.
